title: kbid.py add writes the repository's MIT licence for a gitlab-org/gitlab doc/ page, whose LICENSE puts doc/ under CC BY-SA 4.0
goal: provider.read_licence for a gitlab.com raw or blob url under gitlab-org/gitlab doc/ gives CC BY-SA 4.0 (the repository LICENSE puts all content under doc/ under CC BY-SA 4.0) or reads nothing and leaves the pair to the flags, instead of the repository-wide MIT the GitLab API reports, while a url outside doc/ keeps the API's licence; a stubbed GitLab answer in the kbid licence part of test_live_kb.py's test_lookup_eval_passes_on_the_live_kb proves it (no new test id)

run:
import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'_tools');import provider as p
p.request=lambda *a,**k:{'status':0,'body':b'','headers':{},'final':a[0],'hops':0,'error':'offline'}
p._repository_licence=lambda f,a:(200,'MIT',False,'')
r=p.read_licence('https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/raw/9f1632e2d74cf3c87fce2513c999c6cf84a97ab4/doc/user/project/repository/signed_commits/_index.md')
q=p.read_licence('https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/blob/master/app/models/user.rb')
print(r['licence'],'|',q['licence']);sys.exit(1 if r['licence'].startswith('MIT') or not q['licence'].startswith('MIT') else 0)

gates.question: For a raw, blob or tree url under gitlab-org/gitlab doc/, does provider.read_licence return CC BY-SA 4.0 itself or read nothing and leave the pair to the flags?

A doc/ url whose ref holds a slash (a branch feature/x) cannot be split from its path by pattern: keep the single-segment ref match and let such a url fall to the API's licence, or return unread for any url of the repository whose path holds /doc/?
options: unread when the path holds /doc/ and no match
